goal.problem: scribe/notes.py uses direct JSONL file I/O for all operations. The new folder-per-type storage engine (scribe/store.py from Phase 1) exists but nothing uses it yet.
goal.solution: Rewire all CLI commands in scribe/notes.py to delegate storage operations to ScribeStore, removing the old JSONL read/write code paths.
goal.value: Completes the storage switchover so the CLI produces the new folder-per-type layout, enabling migration (Phase 3) and all downstream phases.

components.name: ScribeStore integration in main()
components.description: Initialize ScribeStore with the resolved state_dir at CLI entry. Pass it to command handlers instead of raw file paths.

components.name: Rewritten cmd_add
components.description: Calls store.add_note() instead of directly appending to notes.jsonl. Handles --content, --type, --session-id, --role, --mission flags as before.

components.name: Rewritten cmd_get / cmd_list / cmd_done / cmd_update / cmd_archive
components.description: Each delegates to the corresponding ScribeStore method. Output format stays identical to current behavior.

components.name: Rewritten cmd_learn / cmd_learnings / cmd_unlearn
components.description: Learning commands delegate to ScribeStore's learning methods. Same CLI surface.

components.name: Rewritten auto-archive logic
components.description: The existing 30-day auto-archive check now calls store.archive_note() which moves entries to archive subfolders instead of a separate archive JSONL.

components.name: Removed old JSONL helpers
components.description: Remove read_jsonl, write_jsonl, make_note, and other direct file I/O functions that are superseded by ScribeStore.

shape.integration_point: scribe/notes.py — full rewrite of storage layer, CLI surface unchanged.
shape.pattern: Existing argparse structure and command dispatch preserved. Only internal implementation changes.
shape.data_flow: CLI args -> argparse -> command handler -> ScribeStore method -> folder/index/file I/O -> stdout output.

behavior.input: Same CLI interface as today: notes.py add --type todo --content '...', notes.py get 306, notes.py list, notes.py done 306, etc.
behavior.processing: 1. main() creates ScribeStore(state_dir). 2. Each cmd_* function receives the store instance. 3. cmd_add calls store.add_note(), prints 'Added #N (type)'. 4. cmd_get calls store.get_note(id), prints metadata + content. 5. cmd_list calls store.list_notes() with filters, prints summary table. 6. cmd_done calls store.update_note(id, status='done'). 7. Auto-archive runs on list/add, calling store.archive_note() for notes older than 30 days. 8. Learning commands call store.add_learning/list_learnings/remove_learning.
behavior.output: Identical CLI output format to current implementation. Same exit codes.

error_cases.behavior: Print error message, exit 1. Same as current behavior.
Argparse rejects it. Add 'general' to the valid choices.

edge_cases.behavior: Merge all type indexes via store.list_notes(type=None).
Rewire to scan handoffs/ index instead of full JSONL.

in_scope: Rewire all cmd_* functions to use ScribeStore
Update scribe/test_notes.py to work with new storage
must_not_break: All existing CLI commands produce identical output format
Backfill agent's ability to call notes.py add --type handoff

acceptance_criteria: Given the new store layout, when 'notes.py add --type todo --content test' is run, then a file appears in todos/ with correct index entry and .md content
Given a note exists with id=5, when 'notes.py get 5' is run, then output matches the format: ID, Type, Status, Session, Time, content
Given notes of mixed types, when 'notes.py list' is run, then all are shown sorted by timestamp with type labels
Given a note with id=5, when 'notes.py done 5' is run, then the index entry status changes to 'done'
Given a note older than 30 days, when any list or add command runs, then the note is auto-archived to the archive/ subfolder
Given 'notes.py learn --content test' is run, then a learning entry appears in learnings/ with correct index and .md file
Given 'notes.py list --type todo --search fix' is run, then only todos with 'fix' in summary are shown
Given 'notes.py show 5' is run (alias), then output is identical to 'notes.py get 5'
Given 'notes.py handoff-sessions' is run, then it lists sessions from handoffs/ index
